key_insight: Concentrating NACA0006 airfoil grids near the pipe wall can suppress turbulence enough to achieve a net drag reduction, increasing flow rate without the usual penalty of added resistance.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical pipe-flow control strategy that could lower pumping power in water and gas distribution systems while maintaining or improving throughput.
method: Axisymmetric RANS simulations with the k-ω SST turbulence model and periodic boundary conditions
Validate the model against fully developed turbulent pipe flow and prior LEBU experiment data
Test concentric-ring airfoil-grid layouts, especially near-wall placement, under fixed pressure difference
evidence_signal: At a pressure difference corresponding to Re ≈ 10^5, the near-wall grid layout increased flow rate by up to 9.0%, reduced area-integrated Reynolds shear stress by 29%, and stayed beneficial across 5×10^4 ≤ Re ≤ 2×10^5.
watch_item: Results are model-based and depend on idealized geometry and boundary conditions, so experimental verification and sensitivity to manufacturing/installation tolerances are still needed.
paper_title: Net drag reduction in turbulent pipe flow by airfoil-section grids concentrated near the wall
